small_guidance:
- The current accumulator tile is OC_C×BLOCK_N = 64×BLOCK_N with a GEMM-K of only IC_C=16 per (kh,kw) — very K-thin dots. Add autotune configs with larger BLOCK_N (256, 512) at num_warps=8, num_stages=2, and try BLOCK_N along the OH·OW combined axis instead of OW only so the program covers more output per launch.
- Collapse the (oh, ow) grid into a single flattened spatial axis (pid_s over OH*OW) and recompute oh, ow inside the kernel; this reduces grid overhead (currently N*OH = 128*126 = 16128 programs) and increases work per program.
- Try ordering the static loops so (kh,kw) is the outer reduction and IC is inner with a wider IC_C padded power-of-two (already 16) — or hoist the (kh,kw)*IC into a single K loop of length KH*KW*IC=72 fed into one tl.dot for better MMA utilization.
large_guidance:
- Rewrite as an explicit im2col-style GEMM: one program per (N, OC tile, output-spatial tile) with BLOCK_M=64 (OC), BLOCK_N=64–128 (spatial), BLOCK_K=32 over the unrolled IC*KH*KW=72 axis. Use a single tl.dot per K step rather than nested static_range over (kh,kw), so tensor cores are fed with proper-shaped tiles.
- Switch input layout to channels_last (NHWC) so the GEMM-K (IC) dimension is contiguous and loads coalesce; weights laid out as (OC, KH, KW, IC) similarly. This is the main throughput lever — the current NCHW gather strides IH*IW between channels and starves memory bandwidth.
- Fuse the BN+scale epilogue directly after the accumulator (already done) and consider a persistent-program scheme over the spatial tile axis so each CTA handles multiple (n, spatial-tile) outputs, amortizing weight loads across batch.
